title: The Sunday Read: “Why Do We Love TikTok Audio Memes? Call it ‘Brainfeel.’”

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson, and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·荣森，欢迎收听《重新构想者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you, and you turned a DJ booth
sentences.zh: 甚至在黑胶唱片时代的夜店当DJ时，你每天晚上也要带着300件最珍爱的宝贝去上班，你会把DJ台

sentences.en: into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 变成这样一个充满生活气息的快闪博物馆，摆满了美丽的、有50年历史的艺术品。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重新构想者》。

sentences.en: I was noticing on TikTok more than I ever had in my life how quickly a sound can get an emotional response out of me.
sentences.zh: 我前所未有地在TikTok上注意到，一种声音能以多快的速度在我心中引发情感共鸣。

sentences.en: It's sort of like if you're attending a wedding and you're not that close to the people who are getting married, but one of them's crying while they're saying their vows,
sentences.zh: 这有点像你去参加婚礼，你和新人们其实并不算太熟，但其中一人在宣誓时哭了，

sentences.en: and it's so moving to hear someone else crying or even to hear their attempt not to cry in their voice that you tear up too.
sentences.zh: 听到别人哭泣，甚至听到他们在声音中努力克制哭腔，是如此感人，以至于你也跟着热泪盈眶。

sentences.en: I think that's clearly true of a lot of people using TikTok, because when you look at the comments, people will write things like,
sentences.zh: 我想这对于许多使用TikTok的人来说显然是真的，因为当你查看评论时，人们会写下这样的东西：

sentences.en: I've never cried so much in my life, or I hope this is what I hear when I get to heaven.
sentences.zh: 我这辈子从来没哭得这么惨过，或者，我希望这就是我上天堂时听到的声音。

sentences.en: And they're saying this about clips that are sometimes less than 10 seconds long.
sentences.zh: 他们对这些有时甚至不到10秒钟的短视频片段发出了这样的感叹。

sentences.en: So it made me think, why are we so affected by sounds on TikTok when those sounds aren't inherently musical or don't have a lot of verbal information?
sentences.zh: 这让我思考，为什么当TikTok上的声音本身并非音乐、也没有包含太多语言信息时，我们还会如此深受其触动？

sentences.en: I'm Charlotte Shane, I write for the New York Times Magazine, and for better or worse, I'm a TikTok enthusiaSt.
sentences.zh: 我是夏洛特·谢恩，我为《纽约时报杂志》撰稿，不管怎样，我是一个TikTok迷。

sentences.en: When you upload a video on TikTok, you can choose to make the audio for that video available for people to reuse as many times as they want.
sentences.zh: 当你上传一个TikTok视频时，你可以选择将该视频的音频开放，供人们无限次重复使用。

sentences.en: So you're essentially packaging it as a meme.
sentences.zh: 所以你本质上是在把它包装成一个表情包。

sentences.en: It's the one where Roger's hiding behind the bar, and the villain, played by Christopher Lloyd, is trying to entice Roger to come out by tapping on the walls, shave, and a haircut.
sentences.zh: 就是罗杰躲在酒吧后面，由克里斯托弗·劳埃德饰演的反派试图通过敲击墙壁来引诱罗杰出来，敲门声是：刮胡子，理个发。

sentences.en: It's sort of like when your favorite song cuts off at the part you were most excited for.
sentences.zh: 这有点像你最喜欢的歌曲在你最兴奋的那一部分突然戛然而止。

sentences.en: They produce a feeling of wanting a sound to complete so badly that you simply have to keep listening.
sentences.zh: 它们会产生一种对声音完整呈现的强烈渴望，以至于你根本不得不继续听下去。

sentences.en: Usually, several times over.
sentences.zh: 通常还得反复听好几遍。

sentences.en: I can't think of many other things in life that create that same intensity with the stakes being so low.
sentences.zh: 我想不出生活中还有什么其他事情能在代价如此之低的情况下产生如此强烈的效果。

sentences.en: So I wanted to figure out, with TikTok being the most popular app in the world, how has it changed our relationship to sound?
sentences.zh: 所以我想要弄清楚，既然TikTok已经是世界上最受欢迎的应用程序，它是如何改变我们与声音的关系的？

sentences.en: The accompanying score, named Primal Fear, was released by Dave James in 2011, and, thanks to Gleason's boost, leads a robustly memed life of its own.

sentences.en: Welcome to the era of the audio meme, a time when replicable units of sound are a cultural currency as strong as, if not stronger than, images and text.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到音频表情包时代，在这个时代里，可复制的声音单元是一种文化货币，其力量不亚于、甚至强于图像和文字。

sentences.en: Though TikTok didn't invent the audio meme, its effortless interface may have perfected it, and the platform, which recently ended

sentences.en: And what a range of sound there is.
